message.content:
Using the standard convention for spherical coordinates \((\rho,\theta,\phi)\):

\[
x=\rho\sin\phi\cos\theta,\qquad z=\rho\cos\phi
\]

Given:
\[
\rho=12,\quad \theta=\frac{2\pi}{3},\quad \phi=\frac{\pi}{4}
\]

Compute:
\[
x=12\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)
=12\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \left(-\frac12\right)
=-3\sqrt{2}
\]

\[
z=12\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)
=12\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}
=6\sqrt{2}
\]

Thus:
\[
x+z=-3\sqrt{2}+6\sqrt{2}=3\sqrt{2}
\]

The answer is \(3\sqrt{2}\).
